impl.summary: Idol 3D can now make the other sides of an object from one picture. A new graph, image-to-views-idol, renders Idol's pruned splat from IdolCamera's predicted camera four times, 90 degrees apart: index 0 is the front (the input view), then the object's left, back and right. A request asks for the views with params.extra.idolViews on oss-idol. The variant resolver (and so the GPU pre-flight gate) then swaps in the view graph. The provider names each picture's side, and the run says plainly when the ComfyUI lacks ComfyUI-Idol or the pack is switched off in Settings. Demo mode answers with four labelled pictures. Image to 3D -> From several images, on your GPU with only the front filled, offers 'Make the other sides from the front (Idol 3D)', which fills the empty left, back and right slots for oss-trellis2-multi. A new character or prop element offers 'Add side and back views'. Both show the price first and say the views are renders of a 3D guess and can look soft, and the note stays once the views are in. Neither shows for guests or accounts, on a paid-APIs-only install, or with Idol 3D switched off. The orbit direction was checked: an asymmetric splat rendered through ComfyUI 0.41.0's own RenderSplat code confirmed that frames +4 puts the object's left at index 1. The shared server in this container had ComfyUI-Idol at the pin (put there by the repo's install-comfyui.sh), and the /prompt check of image-to-views-idol passed. No GPU run.

findings.title: A view run is lost if its button goes away mid-run
findings.detail: OtherSides holds runId in its own state and hands the views over only while it is mounted. In Image to 3D, switching away from From several images (or changing the engine) unmounts it, and the GPU run finishes with nothing handed over. In Elements the same happens when the dialog closes or the kind changes to location or style. Coming back offers the button again, so a second paid or GPU run gets started. Also, if the front photo is replaced mid-run, the views of the old front fill the slots next to the new front. The pictures stay in the helper job, so nothing is corrupted.
findings.verified: Traced from the code: runId is local state, the parent's onBusy cleanup sets busy to false, and nothing re-attaches to a running IDOL_VIEWS_FEATURE job.

findings.title: Elements offers the button when editing an existing element too, not only for a new one
findings.detail: The report says 'A new character or prop element offers...'. offerSides has no !element check, so editing a saved character or prop with photos offers it again, including one whose views were made in an earlier session. This is harmless and arguably useful, but it differs from the report and is not covered by the e2e test.

findings.title: The asymmetric orbit-direction check isn't kept as a test
findings.detail: The unit tests only assert frames: 4 and the index -> side table. The asymmetric-splat render that set the sign was an ad-hoc script and is not committed. I checked the sign by hand: _orbit_camera_info_yaw rotates the camera about world +Y with Ry = [[c,0,s],[0,1,0],[-s,0,c]]. That takes a camera at +Z to +X, the viewer's right, which is the object's left. IdolCamera's camera.py puts the camera in three.js Y-up world, aimed at the object at the origin, and the splat frame map (x,-y,-z) is a rotation, not a mirror. So +4 giving front, left, back, right is correct.

fix.finalSummary: idol-8 lets Idol 3D make the other sides of an object from one picture. image-to-views-idol is the clean Idol graph up to the pruned splat, then RenderSplat from IdolCamera with frames +4 and SaveImage. It returns front, left, back and right, each with meta.index and meta.side. Open engine (your ComfyUI): built and unit-tested, and the /prompt check passed on this container's CPU server, which has ComfyUI-Idol at the pin. Not run on a GPU: it needs a GPU and Idol's weights. Without the pack, the run is refused with a plain message. Image to 3D -> From several images, on your GPU with only the front in, offers 'Make the other sides from the front (Idol 3D)' and fills left, back and right for TRELLIS.2 multi-view. Elements offers 'Add side and back views' for characters and products. Both show the price and say the views are soft renders of a 3D guess. The run is now kept for its picture, so leaving and coming back mid-run picks it up instead of paying twice. Cloud engine: no route. Idol's fal endpoint returns a splat, not views, so the button is hidden on the cloud engine and on paid-APIs-only installs. Demo mode returns four labelled placeholders. Public sign-up: guests don't see the button. Accounts don't either, and POST /api/generations answers 403 own-gpu-tool for their view request (tested), as for every 3D model. Fixed in this stage: the library notes no longer say 'untested' (comfy-library-notes passes), and a view run survives its button unmounting.
